target_customer: E-commerce retailers and marketplaces with large product catalogs
problem: Retailers must categorize and tag millions of products to power search, filtering and recommendations, which is slow and manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS or API for product data categorization and tagging
product_category: e-commerce product data enrichment using computer vision and NLP

founders.name: Sarah Wooders
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no education or employers. Search snippets say the idea began with a fashion search project at MIT, not opened here.

founders.name: Alice Deng
founders.background_notes: YC page also says she led Blueprint and later became co-founder and CPO of Slope.

exit.reason: Cause not public; the YC directory marks the company Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate attribute extraction from product images and text needed computer vision and NLP models, doable by a small team with off-the-shelf research but hard to make accurate across categories.

defensibility.rationale: Models could be copied or built in house by larger retailers; value would depend on accumulated labeled data, which no source shows had accrued.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Glisten; the company went inactive, cause not public.

market_need_then: Online catalogs were growing quickly and product data quality drives search and conversion; Glisten pitched taxonomizing millions of products for better search and recommendations. No dated customer evidence found.

branding.domain_note: Used glisten.ai; a separate unrelated design assistant also uses the Glisten.ai name per search results.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or merch found; only directory listings and a Shopify app page.

outcome_analysis: Glisten AI sold automatic product categorization and tagging to e-commerce retailers and went through the Winter 2020 batch as a one or two person team. Directories show a small seed of roughly 125 to 150 thousand dollars and then no later round. The YC directory marks it Inactive but no shutdown announcement, post-mortem or acquisition notice was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. One of its founders went on to found other companies per the YC page.
notes: glisten.ai did not resolve from this sandbox (DNS failure); not independently confirmed dead. Seed amount conflicts: CB Insights and Bouncewatch say $150K in March 2020, TheCompanyCheck says $125K; no primary source or Form D found, so the round rests on aggregators. Investors Soma Capital from Bouncewatch, Dorm Room Fund from CB Insights. Competitors list left empty: only 2026 pages found for Syndigo, Salsify and similar PIM vendors, nothing dated near the batch. A claim linking Wooders to later AI memory work was in a search summary and is not recorded here. Cause of inactivity not public.
